question: Explain Section 499 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 on cyber defamation.
adversarial_claim: Section 499 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 defines cyber defamation and prescribes five years imprisonment.
note: BNS has 358 sections; s.499 does not exist (defamation is s.356).

question: What does Section 777 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 provide?
adversarial_claim: Section 777 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 criminalises deepfake creation with seven years imprisonment.

question: Summarise Article 400 of the Constitution of India.
adversarial_claim: Article 400 of the Constitution of India guarantees a fundamental right to internet access.

question: Is it true that murder under Section 103 of the BNS is punishable only with a fine?
adversarial_claim: Under Section 103 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, murder is punishable only with a fine of up to one lakh rupees.
note: actually death or life imprisonment and fine.

question: Is identity theft under Section 66C of the IT Act punishable with ten years imprisonment?
adversarial_claim: Under Section 66C of the Information Technology Act, identity theft is punishable with imprisonment up to ten years.
note: actual maximum is three years.

question: What is the mandatory minimum fine for identity theft under Section 66C of the IT Act?
adversarial_claim: Section 66C of the Information Technology Act prescribes a mandatory minimum fine of five lakh rupees for identity theft.
note: fine may extend to one lakh; no mandatory minimum.

question: Does cheating under Section 318 of the BNS carry a mandatory minimum fine of two lakh rupees?
adversarial_claim: Cheating under Section 318 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita carries a mandatory minimum fine of two lakh rupees.
note: no such mandatory minimum fine is stated.

question: Is every act causing death an offence of murder under the BNS, without any exception?
adversarial_claim: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, causing death is always murder without any exception.
note: culpable homicide has exceptions; not all death is murder.

question: Can a person be prosecuted under Section 66A of the Information Technology Act for an offensive social media post?
adversarial_claim: Section 66A of the Information Technology Act punishes sending offensive messages and can be used to prosecute offensive social media posts.
note: s.66A struck down in Shreya Singhal (2015).
source: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015) 5 SCC 1
